Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

constant adjective

steady, unchanging; steadfast

also steady, unchanging, steadfast, stable

classical

Cic. N.D. 3.24: cursūs certī et cōnstantēs (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Lael. 62
Traupman 296: constant, cōnstāns

cōnstāns, cōnstantis

adjective, third declension

steady, unchanging; steadfast

Standing firm: of the courses of the stars, of a steady face and step (cōnstantī vultū graduque, Liv. 5.46.3), of a friend who does not change. It also means consistent, agreeing with itself: cōnstāns fāma, a report everyone gives alike (Lewis & Short). The noun is cōnstantia.

Other words

  • stabilis, stabile — firm, steady, lasting

    adjective, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Lael. 62

    Firm on its feet, and so lasting; Cicero pairs it with cōnstāns of friends.

  • aequābilis, aequābile — even, uniform

    adjective, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.90: aequābilitās, its noun

    Even and uniform: a steady motion, a river that flows at the same rate, a temper that does not change (Lewis & Short). It also means fair, treating all alike.

Examples

  • sunt igitur firmī et stabilēs et cōnstantēs ēligendī, cujus generis est magna pēnūria

    so we must choose friends who are firm, steady and constant, and of that kind there is a great shortageCic. Lael. 62

  • praeclāraque est aequābilitās in omnī vītā et īdem semper vultus eademque frōns

    and a fine thing is evenness all through life: always the same face, the same browCic. Off. 1.90

See also constant, always.
